transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um, I guess I came in because... well, I've been having some trouble communicating lately. I'm an artist, and when I'm writing my artist statements or client notes, or even just talking in meetings, I keep jumping around. 

I'll go from talking about, like, canvas textures, straight into project budgets, and then into these secret meanings behind things. People just keep telling me they can’t follow what I’m trying to explain, and it's making my work really difficult.
Have you experienced any periods where you felt unusually energetic, didn't need much sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing at an intense speed?

Yeah, I have. Um... sometimes when I'm working late, I can sleep for just two or three hours and then wake up feeling really bright and ready to keep right on going. I'm just not tired at all, not the way I normally would be after getting so little rest.
Have you ever experienced moments where you felt like you were hearing or seeing things that others couldn't, even when you weren't feeling particularly energetic or high-spirited?

Yes, I have. Um, there was a quieter month a little while back where I was actually sleeping more normally, and I didn't feel unstoppable or super energetic. But even then, for several weeks, I still kept hearing these comments coming from behind the shelves in my workspace. And I was still reading hidden warnings into just ordinary studio materials. So, yeah, that still happened even when my energy was pretty normal.

Aside from the times when you felt unusually energetic, have you ever gone through a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt persistently sad, hopeless, or lost interest in your art and other activities?

No, I don't think so. Um... I mean, I get frustrated sometimes if a project isn't going well, but I haven't really had a time where I felt persistently sad or hopeless for weeks on end. And I definitely haven't lost interest in my art. Even when I'm dealing with the other stuff I mentioned, I still always want to be in the studio working. So, no, I haven't really experienced anything like that.

During those times when you felt unusually energetic and didn't need much sleep, did you also experience a significant increase in your activity levels, such as starting many new projects or being much more talkative than usual?

Yeah, definitely. When I get like that, my activity level goes way up. I'll suddenly take on, like, three different grant proposals at once. I'll reorganize my entire studio, stay up sketching all night, and send out a bunch of emails to curators. I even start cutting materials for pieces that I haven't budgeted for or really planned out yet. I just can't seem to stop moving or doing things.
During that quieter month when you weren't feeling energetic, did you still find yourself jumping around from topic to topic or having trouble making sense when you spoke to others?

Yeah, actually, that's a big part of why I'm here. Even when my energy was normal, my thoughts were just... everywhere. People keep telling me they can't follow what I'm trying to explain. Like, I'll be in a meeting, or writing up an artist statement or client notes, and I'll jump from talking about the textures of a piece, to the budget, to these secret meanings I'm seeing in the materials. It just all runs together, and I guess it doesn't make sense to anyone else.

Looking back at the past year or so, would you say that the times when you felt that intense energy and need for less sleep happened quite frequently, or were they relatively rare compared to the times when you felt more like your normal self?

I'd say they happened pretty frequently. Actually, um... looking back over this whole period, those energized, kind of irritable and overproductive stretches have definitely taken up more of the year than the calmer stretches. 

The intensity of it kind of rises and falls, you know? It's not always exactly the same. But overall, yeah, I've spent way more time in that high-energy mode than feeling like my normal self.

Could you estimate how long, in total, you have experienced these periods of hearing voices and seeing hidden meanings in things, compared to the amount of time you have spent in those high-energy states?

Um, let me think. The messages I see in the materials, and... well, the voice or those smells I notice in the studio, that's all been happening for roughly 11 months. So, I guess almost the whole year. They've kind of just been going on right alongside all that high energy.

Thinking back over the past year, have there been any periods of at least two weeks where you experienced those voices or hidden meanings, but were NOT feeling that high energy or racing thoughts at the same time?

Yeah, there was. Like I mentioned earlier, there was that one quieter month. I was sleeping more normally then, and I definitely didn't have that unstoppable, racing energy. But even during those few weeks, I was still hearing those comments coming from behind the studio shelves. And I was still seeing those hidden warnings in the materials I was working with. So, yeah, that stuff was still happening even when the energy wasn't there.
Have you ever experienced a significant period of at least two weeks where you felt a complete loss of interest or pleasure in all or almost all of your usual activities?

No, I don't think so. I mean, even during that quieter month I mentioned, I still wanted to be in the studio. I still cared about my art. I haven't really had a time where I just... lost interest in everything for weeks on end. So, no, I wouldn't say I've experienced that.
During any of the times when you were experiencing those voices or hidden meanings, did you ever feel a significant sense of worthlessness, guilt, or have recurring thoughts about death or suicide?

No, I haven't really felt like that. I mean, I've never felt completely worthless or had any thoughts about dying or anything like that. Even when things get a bit overwhelming with the voices or the messages, it doesn't make me feel guilty or down on myself. So, no, I haven't experienced those kinds of thoughts.
